reviews.title: Native 2666 MHz support without having to enable memory overclocking
reviews.comment:
I bought these after suffering a dead on arrival DIMM chip from a name brand memory manufacturer (see my other reviews to see which brand) to go with a new PC build (2020 Gigabyte motherboard, 2020 Intel processor).
The name brand memory showed up in my Bios as 2400 MHz memory, I had to enable the memory overclocking function for the name-brand to show up and function as it was sold (2666 Mhz).  I returned/replaced the name brand memory with this brand because of the dead DIMM chip.  A)  Both chips worked out of the box, unlike the name brand.  B) I didn't have to enable any sort of overclocking in my bios for these to show up and function at the 2666 MHz they are listed as.  And no I didn't just leave memory overclocking on... I shut it off before I removed the other chips.  That other memory should be sold as "Can reach 2666 MHz with overclocking" - this OLOy memory is recognized and functions at 2666 MHz without overclocking enabled.
A quality product at a reasonable price.
reviews.author: Friendly Consumers
